tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

Odd. Could be pip sets restrictive ACL? Or antivirus. We can avoid deps.

Could use web fetch for a word list and definitions. Maybe easiest: download a common English dictionary JSON (e.g., `dictionary.json` from adambom) with ~100k words definitions. Then select common words using a frequency list (also fetch). This can be done with `Invoke-WebRequest` (not pip) into workspace. Need network raw.githubusercontent.com. Let's try fetch a known dictionary.

Known repos:
- https://github.com/adambom/dictionary - `dictionary.json` map of word -> definition? I recall it's ~2.5MB JSON with 80k words, each `{"word": "...", "definition": "..."}`? Actually repo has `dictionary.json` object where values are `{ "word": "...", "definition": "..."}`. It may be from Webster's 1913, definitions old.
- https://github.com/matthewreagan/WebstersEnglishDictionary - `dictionary.json` ~30MB, definitions.
- https://github.com/wordset/wordset-dictionary - data.
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/first20hours/google-10000-english/master/google-10000-english.txt` common words frequency list.
Could fetch 10k list + dictionary, select first N that have definitions, filter. This gives database of 500 common words. Definitions from Webster's can be archaic but okay.
- Better use WordNet via `wn` data file. Could fetch `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/globalwordnet/english-wordnet/master/src/...`? Hard.

Could download NLTK WordNet corpus zip directly: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nltk/nltk_data/gh-pages/packages/corpora/wordnet.zip` (~10MB). Then parse WordNet data. But that's more complex than dictionary JSON. NLTK data also has `wordnet` with `data.noun`, `data.verb`, etc., and `index.*`; parse definitions and synsets. Doable. But need common word frequency list. We can fetch google-10000 list and intersect with WordNet lemmas. WordNet gives POS, definition, synonyms, hypernyms. This would be high quality. Parsing WordNet:
- data.noun lines: `offset lex_filenum ss_type w_cnt word lex_id ... p_cnt ... | gloss`
- Could parse using regex to extract definition after `|`, and lemma names from first part. Synset offset key.
- Need map offset to synset object for hypernyms. Hypernym pointers `@` point to offsets.
- For each word, choose first synset in index by sense number.
Could be done in a preparation script. But maybe overkill.

Alternatively, use `wordfreq` via fetching package source? No.

We can handcraft 100 entries; not too bad and content quality controlled. The user likely won't test thousands. But "database for common English words" suggests more than 20. 100-150 is adequate for demo. Could make 150 with categories.

Yet semantic scoring using curated categories works. Need be careful descriptions. Let's estimate writing 120 entries manually: 7 fields each, maybe 5000 words. Time-consuming but doable. Better generate via dictionary API + word list programmatically, then review.

Let's try fetching google 10k and dictionary.

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build ``words.json`` and ``words.db`` from WordNet and a frequency list.

This is a development-time script.  The game itself only needs the generated
SQLite database and Python's standard library.

Example:

        --wordnet-dir .tmp/wordnet/dict ^
        --frequency common-10000.txt ^
        --limit 650

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

QUOTED_EXAMPLE = re.compile(r'"([^"]+)"')
CLEAN_LEMMA = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z ]{1,34}$")
WORD_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z]{3,13}$")


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Synset:
    offset: str
    pos: str
    lex: str
    lemmas: tuple[str, ...]
    pointers: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    definition: str = ""
    examples: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def _clean_text(text: str) -> str:
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
    text = text.replace("\u2019", "'").replace("\u2018", "'")
    text = text.replace("\u201c", '"').replace("\u201d", '"')
    text = text.replace("\u2013", "-").replace("\u2014", "-")
    return " ".join(text.split())


def _lemma(text: str) -> str:
    return _clean_text(text.replace("_", " ").casefold())


def _parse_gloss(gloss: str) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    gloss = _clean_text(gloss)
    pieces = DEFINITION_SPLIT.split(gloss, maxsplit=1)
    definition = pieces[0].strip()
    examples = tuple(QUOTED_EXAMPLE.findall(gloss))
    return definition, examples


def parse_data(path: Path, pos: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]:
    """Parse one WordNet ``data.*`` file."""
    group = POS_GROUP[pos]
    result: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset] = {}
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            if not line or not line[0].isdigit():
                continue
            head, separator, gloss = line.rstrip("\n").partition(" | ")
            if not separator:
                continue
            fields = head.split()
            if len(fields) < 6:
                continue
            offset, lex, ss_type, raw_count = fields[:4]
            try:
                word_count = int(raw_count, 16)
                pointer_index = 4 + 2 * word_count
                pointer_count = int(fields[pointer_index])
            except (ValueError, IndexError):
                continue
            lemmas = tuple(
                _lemma(fields[4 + 2 * index])
                for index in range(word_count)
            )
            pointers: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
            cursor = pointer_index + 1
            for _ in range(pointer_count):
                if cursor + 3 >= len(fields):
                    break
                symbol = fields[cursor]
                target_offset = fields[cursor + 1]
                target_pos = fields[cursor + 2]
                pointers.append(
                    (symbol, POS_GROUP.get(target_pos, target_pos), target_offset)
                )
                cursor += 4
            definition, examples = _parse_gloss(gloss)
            result[(group, offset)] = Synset(
                offset=offset,
                pos=ss_type,
                lex=lex,
                lemmas=lemmas,
                pointers=pointers,
                definition=definition,
                examples=examples,
            )
    return result


def parse_index(path: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]]:
    result: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            fields = line.strip().split()
            if len(fields) < 6:
                continue
            lemma = _lemma(fields[0])
            pos = fields[1]
            if pos not in POS_GROUP:
                continue
            try:
                count = int(fields[2])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            offsets = tuple(fields[-count:])
            if len(offsets) == count and all(
                offset.isdigit() for offset in offsets
            ):
                result[(lemma, pos)] = offsets
    return result


def parse_sense_counts(path: Path) -> Counter[tuple[str, str]]:
    counts: Counter[tuple[str, str]] = Counter()
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            fields = line.split()
            if len(fields) < 4 or "%" not in fields[0]:
                continue
            key = fields[0]
            try:
                tags = int(fields[3])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            lemma, tail = key.split("%", 1)
            pos_number = tail.split(":", 1)[0]
            pos = SENSE_POS.get(pos_number)
            if pos:
                counts[(_lemma(lemma), pos)] += tags
    return counts


def load_synsets(directory: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]:
    synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset] = {}
    for filename, pos in (
        ("data.noun", "n"),
        ("data.verb", "v"),
        ("data.adj", "a"),
        ("data.adv", "r"),
    ):
        synsets.update(parse_data(directory / filename, pos))
    return synsets


def load_indexes(directory: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]]:
    indexes: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    for filename in ("index.noun", "index.verb", "index.adj", "index.adv"):
        indexes.update(parse_index(directory / filename))
    return indexes


def load_frequency(path: Path) -> dict[str, int]:
    ranks: dict[str, int] = {}
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for rank, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
            word = line.strip().casefold()
            if WORD_RE.fullmatch(word) and word not in ranks:
                ranks[word] = rank
    return ranks


def _category_for(
    synset: Synset, synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]
) -> str:
    base = LEX_CATEGORY.get(synset.lex, "Concept")
    if synset.pos not in ("n", "s") or base not in (
        "Artifact",
        "Object",
        "Concept",
    ):
        return base

    ancestors = _ancestor_lemmas(synset, synsets, depth=7)
    for needle, label in REFINE_RULES:
        if needle in ancestors:
            return label
    if base == "Object" and "natural object" in ancestors:
        return "Nature"
    return base


def _hypernyms(
    synset: Synset, synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]
) -> list[Synset]:
    found: list[Synset] = []
    for symbol, pos, offset in synset.pointers:
        if symbol in ("@", "@i") and pos == POS_GROUP.get(synset.pos, synset.pos):
            target = synsets.get((pos, offset))
            if target is not None:
                found.append(target)
    return found


def _ancestor_lemmas(
    synset: Synset,
    synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset],
    depth: int,
) -> set[str]:
    names: set[str] = set()
    frontier = [(synset, 0)]
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = {(POS_GROUP.get(synset.pos, synset.pos), synset.offset)}
    while frontier:
        current, level = frontier.pop()
        if level >= depth:
            continue
        for parent in _hypernyms(current, synsets):
            key = (POS_GROUP.get(parent.pos, parent.pos), parent.offset)
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            names.update(parent.lemmas)
            frontier.append((parent, level + 1))
    return names


def _clean_lemma_list(
    lemmas: tuple[str, ...] | list[str],
    *,
    exclude: set[str],
    limit: int,
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    output: list[str] = []
    for raw in lemmas:
        value = _lemma(raw)
        if value in exclude or value in GENERIC_RELATED:
            continue
        if not CLEAN_LEMMA.fullmatch(value) or value in STOP_WORDS:
            continue
        if len(value.split()) > 3:
            continue
        if value not in output:
            output.append(value)
        if len(output) >= limit:
            break
    return tuple(output)


def _related_for(
    synset: Synset, synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset], exclude: set[str]
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    candidates: list[str] = []
    seen_synsets: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    frontier: list[tuple[Synset, int]] = [(synset, 0)]
    while frontier and len(candidates) < 12:
        current, level = frontier.pop(0)
        if level >= 3:
            continue
        for parent in _hypernyms(current, synsets):
            key = (POS_GROUP.get(parent.pos, parent.pos), parent.offset)
            if key in seen_synsets:
                continue
            seen_synsets.add(key)
            candidates.extend(parent.lemmas)
            frontier.append((parent, level + 1))

    for symbol, pos, offset in synset.pointers:
        if symbol in ("&", "^", "+", "=", ">"):
            target = synsets.get((pos, offset))
            if target is not None:
                candidates.extend(target.lemmas)

    return _clean_lemma_list(
        candidates, exclude=exclude, limit=8
    )


def choose_synset(
    word: str,
    indexes: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]],
    synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset],
    sense_counts: Counter[tuple[str, str]],
) -> Synset | None:
    options: list[tuple[int, int, Synset]] = []
    for pos in ("n", "v", "a", "r"):
        offsets = indexes.get((word, pos))
        if not offsets:
            continue
        synset = synsets.get((pos, offsets[0]))
        if synset is None:
            continue
        options.append((sense_counts.get((word, pos), 0), POS_PRIORITY[pos], synset))
    if not options:
        return None
    options.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
    return options[0][2]


def _valid_definition(word: str, definition: str) -> bool:
    if not definition or not 20 <= len(definition) <= 230:
        return False
    lowered = definition.casefold()
    if re.search(rf"(?<![a-z]){re.escape(word)}(?![a-z])", lowered):
        return False
    if any(marker in lowered for marker in BAD_DEFINITION_MARKERS):
        return False
    if definition.count("(") > 3 or definition.count(")") > 3:
        return False
    if "[" in definition or "]" in definition:
        return False
    if not re.search(r"[a-z]", definition):
        return False
    return True


def build(
    wordnet_dir: Path,
    frequency_path: Path,
    output_path: Path,
    db_path: Path,
    limit: int,
    max_rank: int,
) -> list[dict]:
    print("Parsing WordNet...")
    synsets = load_synsets(wordnet_dir)
    indexes = load_indexes(wordnet_dir)
    sense_counts = parse_sense_counts(wordnet_dir / "index.sense")
    frequency = load_frequency(frequency_path)
    print(f"  {len(synsets):,} synsets, {len(indexes):,} index entries")

    selected: list[dict] = []
    used_words: set[str] = set()
    used_synsets: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    category_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()

    for word in sorted(frequency, key=lambda item: frequency[item]):
        rank = frequency[word]
        if rank > max_rank or len(selected) >= limit:
            break
        if word in STOP_WORDS or word in BLOCK_WORDS or word in used_words:
            continue
        synset = choose_synset(word, indexes, synsets, sense_counts)
        if synset is None:
            continue
        synset_key = (POS_GROUP.get(synset.pos, synset.pos), synset.offset)
        if synset_key in used_synsets:
            continue
        definition = _clean_text(synset.definition)
        if not _valid_definition(word, definition):
            continue

        category = _category_for(synset, synsets)
        synonyms = _clean_lemma_list(
            [lemma for lemma in synset.lemmas if lemma != word],
            exclude={word},
            limit=4,
        )
        related = _related_for(
            synset, synsets, exclude={word, *synonyms}
        )
        if not related:
            related = _clean_lemma_list(
                [lemma for lemma in synset.lemmas if lemma != word],
                exclude={word},
                limit=8,
            )

        difficulty = "easy" if rank <= 1200 else "medium" if rank <= 3500 else "hard"
        selected.append(
            {
                "word": word,
                "pos": synset.pos,
                "definition": definition,
                "category": category,
                "synonyms": list(synonyms),
                "related": list(related),
                "example": synset.examples[0] if synset.examples else "",
                "difficulty": difficulty,
                "frequency_rank": rank,
            }
        )
        used_words.add(word)
        used_synsets.add(synset_key)
        category_counts[category] += 1

    print(f"Selected {len(selected)} words")
    print("Categories:")
    for category, count in category_counts.most_common():
        print(f"  {category:<20} {count:>4}")
    difficulty_counts = Counter(item["difficulty"] for item in selected)
    print("Difficulty:", dict(difficulty_counts))

    payload = {
        "metadata": {
            "name": "Word Sleuth common English words",
            "wordnet_version": "3.0",
            "wordnet_copyright": "Copyright 2006 by Princeton University",
            "frequency_list": "google-10000-english",
            "word_count": str(len(selected)),
        },
        "words": selected,
    }
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
        handle.write("\n")
    build_database(output_path, db_path)
    print(f"Wrote {output_path}")
    print(f"Wrote {db_path}")
    return selected


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--wordnet-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(".tmp/wordnet/dict"),
        help="directory containing WordNet data.* and index.* files",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--frequency",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("common-10000.txt"),
        help="newline-separated English words in frequency order",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--limit", type=int, default=650, help="maximum number of words"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-rank",
        type=int,
        default=7000,
        help="only consider words at or above this frequency rank",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=ROOT / "wordgame" / "data" / "words.json",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=ROOT / "wordgame" / "data" / "words.db",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not args.wordnet_dir.is_dir():
        parser.error(f"WordNet directory not found: {args.wordnet_dir}")
    if not args.frequency.is_file():
        parser.error(f"Frequency list not found: {args.frequency}")
    build(
        args.wordnet_dir,
        args.frequency,
        args.output,
        args.db,
        args.limit,
        args.max_rank,
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build ``words.json`` and ``words.db`` from WordNet and a frequency list.

This is a development-time script.  The game itself only needs the generated
SQLite database and Python's standard library.

Example:
    python tools/build_dataset.py ^
        --wordnet-dir .tmp/wordnet/dict ^
        --frequency common-10000.txt ^
        --limit 650

WordNet 3.0 is available from https://wordnet.princeton.edu/.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from wordgame.database import build_database  # noqa: E402

POS_GROUP = {"n": "n", "v": "v", "a": "a", "s": "a", "r": "r"}
POS_PRIORITY = {"n": 0, "v": 1, "a": 2, "r": 3}
SENSE_POS = {"1": "n", "2": "v", "3": "a", "4": "r", "5": "a"}

LEX_CATEGORY = {
    "03": "Concept",
    "04": "Action",
    "05": "Animal",
    "06": "Artifact",
    "07": "Quality",
    "08": "Body Part",
    "09": "Idea",
    "10": "Communication",
    "11": "Event",
    "12": "Feeling",
    "13": "Food",
    "14": "Group",
    "15": "Place",
    "16": "Motive",
    "17": "Object",
    "18": "Person",
    "19": "Nature",
    "20": "Plant",
    "21": "Possession",
    "22": "Process",
    "23": "Measure",
    "24": "Relation",
    "25": "Shape",
    "26": "State",
    "27": "Material",
    "28": "Time",
    "29": "Body Action",
    "30": "Change",
    "31": "Thinking",
    "32": "Communication",
    "33": "Competition",
    "34": "Consumption",
    "35": "Contact",
    "36": "Creation",
    "37": "Emotion",
    "38": "Movement",
    "39": "Perception",
    "40": "Possession",
    "41": "Social",
    "42": "State",
    "43": "Weather",
    "00": "Description",
    "01": "Related",
    "02": "Manner",
    "44": "Description",
}

# For artifacts and other broad categories, a nearby hypernym gives a much
# more useful clue than "Artifact".
REFINE_RULES = (
    ("vehicle", "Vehicle"),
    ("motor vehicle", "Vehicle"),
    ("furniture", "Furniture"),
    ("clothing", "Clothing"),
    ("garment", "Clothing"),
    ("footwear", "Clothing"),
    ("headwear", "Clothing"),
    ("tool", "Tool"),
    ("weapon", "Weapon"),
    ("projectile", "Weapon"),
    ("container", "Container"),
    ("receptacle", "Container"),
    ("building", "Building"),
    ("edifice", "Building"),
    ("musical instrument", "Instrument"),
    ("instrument", "Instrument"),
    ("machine", "Machine"),
    ("device", "Device"),
    ("appliance", "Appliance"),
    ("toy", "Toy"),
    ("game", "Game"),
    ("sport", "Sport"),
    ("food", "Food"),
    ("dish", "Food"),
    ("beverage", "Drink"),
    ("drink", "Drink"),
    ("book", "Book"),
    ("writing", "Writing"),
    ("currency", "Money"),
    ("money", "Money"),
    ("fabric", "Fabric"),
    ("cloth", "Fabric"),
    ("jewelry", "Jewelry"),
)

STOP_WORDS = frozenset(
    """
    a about above after again against all almost along also although always am
    among an and another any anybody anyone anything are area around as at be
    because been before being below between both but by can cannot could did do
    does doing done down during each either else enough especially etc even ever
    every everyone everything except far few first for from further get gets
    getting give given go goes going good got had has have having he her here
    hers herself him himself his how however i if in into is it its itself just
    keep know last least less let like likely long made make makes making many
    may me might more most mostly much must my myself near need never new next
    no nor not now of off often on once one only or other others our ours
    ourselves out over own per perhaps put quite rather really same say says
    see seem seems several shall she should show side since so some someone
    something sometimes still such sure take than that the their theirs them
    themselves then there these they thing things think this those though
    through thus time to too toward two under until up upon us use used using
    very via want was way we well were what when where whether which while who
    whom whose why will with within without would yes yet you your yours
    yourself yourselves
    """.split()
)

BLOCK_WORDS = frozenset(
    """
    anal anus ass bastard bitch breasts butt cock cunt damn dick dildo fuck
    homosexual intercourse nazi naked nipple orgasm penis porn pornography
    prostitute pussy rape sex sexual shit slut sperm vagina whore xxx
    """.split()
)

BAD_DEFINITION_MARKERS = (
    "obscene",
    "vulgar",
    "profane",
    "sexual intercourse",
    "sexual activity",
)

GENERIC_RELATED = frozenset(
    """
    entity physical entity abstraction thing object whole unit living thing
    organism being causal agent cause physical object matter
    """.split()
)

DEFINITION_SPLIT = re.compile(r";\s+[\"']")
QUOTED_EXAMPLE = re.compile(r'"([^"]+)"')
CLEAN_LEMMA = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z ]{1,34}$")
WORD_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z]{3,13}$")


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Synset:
    offset: str
    pos: str
    lex: str
    lemmas: tuple[str, ...]
    pointers: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    definition: str = ""
    examples: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def _clean_text(text: str) -> str:
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
    text = text.replace("\u2019", "'").replace("\u2018", "'")
    text = text.replace("\u201c", '"').replace("\u201d", '"')
    text = text.replace("\u2013", "-").replace("\u2014", "-")
    return " ".join(text.split())


def _lemma(text: str) -> str:
    return _clean_text(text.replace("_", " ").casefold())


def _parse_gloss(gloss: str) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    gloss = _clean_text(gloss)
    pieces = DEFINITION_SPLIT.split(gloss, maxsplit=1)
    definition = pieces[0].strip()
    examples = tuple(QUOTED_EXAMPLE.findall(gloss))
    return definition, examples


def parse_data(path: Path, pos: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]:
    """Parse one WordNet ``data.*`` file."""
    group = POS_GROUP[pos]
    result: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset] = {}
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            if not line or not line[0].isdigit():
                continue
            head, separator, gloss = line.rstrip("\n").partition(" | ")
            if not separator:
                continue
            fields = head.split()
            if len(fields) < 6:
                continue
            offset, lex, ss_type, raw_count = fields[:4]
            try:
                word_count = int(raw_count, 16)
                pointer_index = 4 + 2 * word_count
                pointer_count = int(fields[pointer_index])
            except (ValueError, IndexError):
                continue
            lemmas = tuple(
                _lemma(fields[4 + 2 * index])
                for index in range(word_count)
            )
            pointers: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
            cursor = pointer_index + 1
            for _ in range(pointer_count):
                if cursor + 3 >= len(fields):
                    break
                symbol = fields[cursor]
                target_offset = fields[cursor + 1]
                target_pos = fields[cursor + 2]
                pointers.append(
                    (symbol, POS_GROUP.get(target_pos, target_pos), target_offset)
                )
                cursor += 4
            definition, examples = _parse_gloss(gloss)
            result[(group, offset)] = Synset(
                offset=offset,
                pos=ss_type,
                lex=lex,
                lemmas=lemmas,
                pointers=pointers,
                definition=definition,
                examples=examples,
            )
    return result


def parse_index(path: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]]:
    result: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            fields = line.strip().split()
            if len(fields) < 6:
                continue
            lemma = _lemma(fields[0])
            pos = fields[1]
            if pos not in POS_GROUP:
                continue
            try:
                count = int(fields[2])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            offsets = tuple(fields[-count:])
            if len(offsets) == count and all(
                offset.isdigit() for offset in offsets
            ):
                result[(lemma, pos)] = offsets
    return result


def parse_sense_counts(path: Path) -> Counter[tuple[str, str]]:
    counts: Counter[tuple[str, str]] = Counter()
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            fields = line.split()
            if len(fields) < 4 or "%" not in fields[0]:
                continue
            key = fields[0]
            try:
                tags = int(fields[3])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            lemma, tail = key.split("%", 1)
            pos_number = tail.split(":", 1)[0]
            pos = SENSE_POS.get(pos_number)
            if pos:
                counts[(_lemma(lemma), pos)] += tags
    return counts


def load_synsets(directory: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]:
    synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset] = {}
    for filename, pos in (
        ("data.noun", "n"),
        ("data.verb", "v"),
        ("data.adj", "a"),
        ("data.adv", "r"),
    ):

    return synsets


def load_indexes(directory: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]]:

    for filename in ("index.noun", "index.verb", "index.adj", "index.adv"):

def load_frequency(path: Path) -> dict[str, int]:

            word = line.strip().casefold()
            if WORD_RE.fullmatch(word) and word not in ranks:
                ranks[word] = rank
    return ranks

    synset: Synset, synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]
) -> str:
    base = LEX_CATEGORY.get(synset.lex, "Concept")

        "Artifact",
        "Object",
        "Concept",
    ):
        return base

    ancestors = _ancestor_lemmas(synset, synsets, depth=7)
    for needle, label in REFINE_RULES:
        if needle in ancestors:
            return label
    if base == "Object" and "natural object" in ancestors:
        return "Nature"
    return base


def _hypernyms(
    synset: Synset, synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset]
) -> list[Synset]:
    found: list[Synset] = []
    for symbol, pos, offset in synset.pointers:
        if symbol in ("@", "@i") and pos == POS_GROUP.get(synset.pos, synset.pos):
            target = synsets.get((pos, offset))
            if target is not None:
                found.append(target)
    return found


def _ancestor_lemmas(
    synset: Synset,
    synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset],
    depth: int,
) -> set[str]:
    names: set[str] = set()
    frontier = [(synset, 0)]
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = {(POS_GROUP.get(synset.pos, synset.pos), synset.offset)}
    while frontier:
        current, level = frontier.pop()
        if level >= depth:
            continue
        for parent in _hypernyms(current, synsets):
            key = (POS_GROUP.get(parent.pos, parent.pos), parent.offset)
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            names.update(parent.lemmas)
            frontier.append((parent, level + 1))
    return names


def _clean_lemma_list(
    lemmas: tuple[str, ...] | list[str],

    exclude: set[str],
    limit: int,

    for raw in lemmas:
        value = _lemma(raw)

            continue

            continue
        if len(value.split()) > 3:

def choose_synset(

def _valid_definition(word: str, definition: str) -> bool:
    if not definition or not 20 <= len(definition) <= 230:

        return False
    if any(marker in lowered for marker in BAD_DEFINITION_MARKERS):

        return False

def build(

    output_path: Path,

    synsets = load_synsets(wordnet_dir)
    indexes = load_indexes(wordnet_dir)

    selected: list[dict] = []
    used_words: set[str] = set()
    used_synsets: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    category_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()

        related = _related_for(
            synset, synsets, exclude={word, *synonyms}
        )
        if not related:

                [lemma for lemma in synset.lemmas if lemma != word],
                exclude={word},
                limit=8,
            )

        difficulty = "easy" if rank <= 1200 else "medium" if rank <= 3500 else "hard"
        selected.append(
            {
                "word": word,
                "pos": synset.pos,
                "definition": definition,
                "category": category,
                "synonyms": list(synonyms),
                "related": list(related),
                "example": synset.examples[0] if synset.examples else "",
                "difficulty": difficulty,
                "frequency_rank": rank,
            }
        )
        used_words.add(word)
        used_synsets.add(synset_key)
        category_counts[category] += 1

    print(f"Selected {len(selected)} words")
    print("Categories:")
    for category, count in category_counts.most_common():
        print(f"  {category:<20} {count:>4}")
    difficulty_counts = Counter(item["difficulty"] for item in selected)
    print("Difficulty:", dict(difficulty_counts))

    payload = {
        "metadata": {
            "name": "Word Sleuth common English words",
            "wordnet_version": "3.0",
            "wordnet_copyright": "Copyright 2006 by Princeton University",
            "frequency_list": "google-10000-english",
            "word_count": str(len(selected)),
        },
        "words": selected,
    }
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
        handle.write("\n")
    build_database(output_path, db_path)
    print(f"Wrote {output_path}")
    print(f"Wrote {db_path}")
    return selected


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--wordnet-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(".tmp/wordnet/dict"),
        help="directory containing WordNet data.* and index.* files",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--frequency",

    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        type=Path,

    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=ROOT / "wordgame" / "data" / "words.db",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not args.wordnet_dir.is_dir():

    if not args.frequency.is_file():

        if symbol in ("&", "^", "+", "=", ">"):
            target = synsets.get((pos, offset))
            if target is not None:
                candidates.extend(target.lemmas)

    return _clean_lemma_list(
        candidates, exclude=exclude, limit=8
    )


def choose_synset(
    word: str,
    indexes: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, ...]],
    synsets: dict[tuple[str, str], Synset],
    sense_counts: Counter[tuple[str, str]],
) -> Synset | None:
    options: list[tuple[int, int, Synset]] = []
    for pos in ("n", "v", "a", "r"):
        offsets = indexes.get((word, pos))
        if not offsets:
            continue
        synset = synsets.get((pos, offsets[0]))
        if synset is None:
            continue
        options.append((sense_counts.get((word, pos), 0), POS_PRIORITY[pos], synset))
    if not options:
        return None
    options.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
    return options[0][2]


def _valid_definition(word: str, definition: str) -> bool:
    if not definition or not 20 <= len(definition) <= 230:
        return False
    lowered = definition.casefold()
    if re.search(rf"(?<![a-z]){re.escape(word)}(?![a-z])", lowered):
        return False
    if any(marker in lowered for marker in BAD_DEFINITION_MARKERS):
        return False
    if definition.count("(") > 3 or definition.count(")") > 3:
        return False
    if "[" in definition or "]" in definition:
        return False
    if not re.search(r"[a-z]", definition):
        return False
    return True


def build(
    wordnet_dir: Path,
    frequency_path: Path,
    output_path: Path,
    db_path: Path,
    limit: int,
    max_rank: int,
) -> list[dict]:
    print("Parsing WordNet...")
    synsets = load_synsets(wordnet_dir)
    indexes = load_indexes(wordnet_dir)
    sense_counts = parse_sense_counts(wordnet_dir / "index.sense")
    frequency = load_frequency(frequency_path)
    print(f"  {len(synsets):,} synsets, {len(indexes):,} index entries")

    selected: list[dict] = []
    used_words: set[str] = set()
    used_synsets: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    category_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()

    for word in sorted(frequency, key=lambda item: frequency[item]):
        rank = frequency[word]
        if rank > max_rank or len(selected) >= limit:
            break
        if word in STOP_WORDS or word in BLOCK_WORDS or word in used_words:
            continue
        synset = choose_synset(word, indexes, synsets, sense_counts)
        if synset is None:
            continue
        synset_key = (POS_GROUP.get(synset.pos, synset.pos), synset.offset)
        if synset_key in used_synsets:
            continue
        definition = _clean_text(synset.definition)
        if not _valid_definition(word, definition):
            continue

        category = _category_for(synset, synsets)
        synonyms = _clean_lemma_list(
            [lemma for lemma in synset.lemmas if lemma != word],
            exclude={word},
            limit=4,
        )
        related = _related_for(
            synset, synsets, exclude={word, *synonyms}
        )
        if not related:
            related = _clean_lemma_list(
                [lemma for lemma in synset.lemmas if lemma != word],
                exclude={word},
                limit=8,
            )

        difficulty = "easy" if rank <= 1200 else "medium" if rank <= 3500 else "hard"
        selected.append(
            {
                "word": word,
                "pos": synset.pos,
                "definition": definition,
                "category": category,
                "synonyms": list(synonyms),
                "related": list(related),
                "example": synset.examples[0] if synset.examples else "",
                "difficulty": difficulty,
                "frequency_rank": rank,
            }
        )
        used_words.add(word)
        used_synsets.add(synset_key)
        category_counts[category] += 1

    print(f"Selected {len(selected)} words")
    print("Categories:")
    for category, count in category_counts.most_common():
        print(f"  {category:<20} {count:>4}")
    difficulty_counts = Counter(item["difficulty"] for item in selected)
    print("Difficulty:", dict(difficulty_counts))

    payload = {
        "metadata": {
            "name": "Word Sleuth common English words",
            "wordnet_version": "3.0",
            "wordnet_copyright": "Copyright 2006 by Princeton University",
            "frequency_list": "google-10000-english",
            "word_count": str(len(selected)),
        },
        "words": selected,
    }
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
        handle.write("\n")
    build_database(output_path, db_path)
    print(f"Wrote {output_path}")
    print(f"Wrote {db_path}")
    return selected


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--wordnet-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(".tmp/wordnet/dict"),
        help="directory containing WordNet data.* and index.* files",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--frequency",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("common-10000.txt"),
        help="newline-separated English words in frequency order",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--limit", type=int, default=650, help="maximum number of words"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-rank",
        type=int,
        default=7000,
        help="only consider words at or above this frequency rank",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=ROOT / "wordgame" / "data" / "words.json",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=ROOT / "wordgame" / "data" / "words.db",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not args.wordnet_dir.is_dir():
        parser.error(f"WordNet directory not found: {args.wordnet_dir}")
    if not args.frequency.is_file():
        parser.error(f"Frequency list not found: {args.frequency}")
    build(
        args.wordnet_dir,
        args.frequency,
        args.output,
        args.db,
        args.limit,
        args.max_rank,
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

{"content": "from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from wordgame.database import (  # noqa: E402
    WordEntry,
    WordRepository,
    build_database,
)
from wordgame.description import describe, hint  # noqa: E402
from wordgame.game import Round, score_label  # noqa: E402
from wordgame.similarity import SemanticScorer  # noqa: E402


class DatabaseTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo = WordRepository()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo.close()

    def test_database_is_seeded(self) -> None:
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(self.repo), 600)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.repo), 700)

    def test_core_categories_exist(self) -> None:
        categories = set(self.repo.categories())
        for expected in ("Animal", "Food", "Vehicle", "Artifact", "Person"):
            self.assertIn(expected, categories)

    def test_lookup_and_alias(self) -> None:
        car = self.repo.get("car")
        self.assertIsNotNone(car)
        assert car is not None
        self.assertEqual(car.category, "Vehicle")
        self.assertIn("auto", {item.casefold() for item in car.synonyms})
        self.assertEqual(self.repo.candidates("auto")[0].word, "car")
        self.assertEqual(self.repo.get("cars").word, "car")

    def test_sampling_is_deterministic_with_seed(self) -> None:
        first = self.repo.sample(random.Random(123), category="Animal")
        second = self.repo.sample(random.Random(123), category="Animal")
        self.assertEqual(first.word, second.word)
        self.assertEqual(first.category, "Animal")

    def test_build_database_from_seed(self) -> None:
        words = [
            {
                "word": "test",
                "pos": "n",
                "definition": "a procedure for checking something",
                "category": "Action",
                "synonyms": ["trial"],
                "related": ["check"],
                "difficulty": "easy",
                "frequency_rank": 1,
            },
            {
                "word": "check",
                "pos": "v",
                "definition": "to inspect or verify something",
                "category": "Action",
                "synonyms": ["verify"],
                "related": ["test"],
                "difficulty": "easy",
                "frequency_rank": 2,
            },
        ]
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            seed = Path(directory) / "seed.json"
            database = Path(directory) / "words.db"
            seed.write_text(json.dumps({"words": words}), encoding="utf-8")
            build_database(seed, database)
            with WordRepository(database) as repo:
                self.assertEqual(len(repo), 2)
                self.assertEqual(repo.get("trial").word, "test")


class DescriptionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo = WordRepository()
        cls.scorer = SemanticScorer(cls.repo.entries)

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo.close()

    def test_description_does_not_leak_answer(self) -> None:
        for word in ("cat", "dog", "car", "apple", "happy"):
            entry = self.repo.get(word)
            assert entry is not None
            text = describe(entry)
            self.assertIsNone(
                __import__("re").search(
                    rf"(?<![a-z]){word}(?:s|es|ed|ing)?(?![a-z])",
                    text.casefold(),
                ),
                f"{word!r} leaked in: {text}",
            )
            self.assertIn(str(entry.letter_count), text)

    def test_adjectives_do_not_get_a_redundant_category(self) -> None:
        entry = self.repo.get("happy")
        assert entry is not None
        text = describe(entry)
        self.assertIn("adjective", text)
        self.assertNotIn("Description category", text)

    def test_hint_reveals_first_letter(self) -> None:
        entry = self.repo.get("cat")
        assert entry is not None
        self.assertIn("'C'", hint(entry, 0))
        self.assertIn("used your hint", hint(entry, 1))


class SimilarityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo = WordRepository()
        cls.scorer = SemanticScorer(cls.repo.entries)

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo.close()

    def _target(self, word: str) -> WordEntry:
        entry = self.repo.get(word)
        assert entry is not None
        return entry

    def test_exact_guess_scores_perfectly(self) -> None:
        result = self.scorer.score(self._target("cat"), "cat", self.repo)
        self.assertTrue(result.correct)
        self.assertEqual(result.points, 100.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(result.cosine, 1.0)

    def test_synonym_scores_perfectly(self) -> None:
        result = self.scorer.score(self._target("car"), "automobile", self.repo)
        self.assertTrue(result.correct)
        self.assertEqual(result.points, 100.0)

    def test_semantically_related_beats_unrelated(self) -> None:
        cat = self._target("cat")
        dog = self.scorer.score(cat, "dog", self.repo)
        car = self.scorer.score(cat, "car", self.repo)
        self.assertGreater(dog.points, car.points + 10)
        self.assertGreater(dog.points, 15)

    def test_similarity_is_symmetric(self) -> None:
        cat = self._target("cat")
        dog = self._target("dog")
        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            self.scorer.similarity(cat, dog),
            self.scorer.similarity(dog, cat),
        )

    def test_unknown_word_is_reported(self) -> None:
        result = self.scorer.score(self._target("cat"), "zzzznotaword", self.repo)
        self.assertFalse(result.known)
        self.assertFalse(result.correct)
        self.assertEqual(result.points, 0.0)

    def test_score_labels(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(score_label(100), "PERFECT")
        self.assertEqual(score_label(75), "Hot")
        self.assertEqual(score_label(0), "Freezing")


class RoundTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo = WordRepository()
        cls.scorer = SemanticScorer(cls.repo.entries)

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls) -> None:
        cls.repo.close()

    def _round(self, word: str = "cat", max_guesses: int = 4) -> Round:
        target = self.repo.get(word)
        assert target is not None
        return Round(target, self.scorer, self.repo, max_guesses=max_guesses)

    def test_duplicate_guess_does_not_use_a_turn(self) -> None:
        round_ = self._round()
        first = round_.guess("dog")
        duplicate = round_.guess("DOG")
        self.assertFalse(first.duplicate)
        self.assertTrue(duplicate.duplicate)
        self.assertEqual(round_.guesses_used, 1)

    def test_correct_guess_finishes_round(self) -> None:
        round_ = self._round()
        outcome = round_.guess("cat")
        self.assertTrue(outcome.result.correct)
        self.assertTrue(round_.finished)
        self.assertTrue(round_.won)

    def test_max_guesses_finishes_round(self) -> None:
        round_ = self._round(max_guesses=2)
        round_.guess("dog")
        round_.guess("lion")
        self.assertTrue(round_.finished)
        self.assertFalse(round_.won)

    def test_hint_is_limited(self) -> None:
        round_ = self._round()
        self.assertIsNotNone(round_.use_hint())
        self.assertIsNone(round_.use_hint())

    def test_give_up(self) -> None:
        round_ = self._round()
        round_.give_up()
        self.assertTrue(round_.finished)
        self.assertTrue(round_.gave_up)
        self.assertIn("CAT", round_.result_line)


class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _run(self, args: list[str], inputs: str = "") -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        environment = dict(__import__("os").environ)
        environment["PYTHONIOENCODING"] = "utf-8"
        environment["NO_COLOR"] = "1"
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "word_guessing.py"), *args],
            input=inputs,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
            timeout=30,
            cwd=ROOT,
            env=environment,
        )

    def test_stats_command(self) -> None:
        completed = self._run(["--stats", "--no-color"])
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        self.assertIn("Words: 700", completed.stdout)
        self.assertIn("Animal", completed.stdout)

    def test_scripted_win(self) -> None:
        completed = self._run(
            ["--word", "car", "--guesses", "3", "--no-color"],
            "automobile\nn\n",
        )
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        self.assertIn("100.0/100", completed.stdout)
        self.assertIn("Solved on the first guess", completed.stdout)
        self.assertIn("Session: 1/1 solved", completed.stdout)

    def test_scripted_loss(self) -> None:
        completed = self._run(
            ["--word", "cat", "--guesses", "1", "--no-color"],
            "car\nn\n",
        )
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        self.assertIn("Out of guesses", completed.stdout)
        self.assertIn("CAT", completed.stdout)

    def test_unknown_forced_word_fails_cleanly(self) -> None:
        completed = self._run(["--word", "zzzznotaword", "--no-color"])
        self.assertNotEqual(completed.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("not in the database", completed.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

content.arguments:
{"content": "# Word Sleuth

A self-contained terminal word-guessing game with a real word database and
cosine-similarity scoring.

The computer picks a common English word, writes a clue from the word's
definition, and asks you to guess. Every guess is scored by how close its
meaning is to the secret word — not just whether it is right or wrong.

```
  WORD SLEUTH
  a semantic word-guessing game
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  700 common English words | TF-IDF cosine scoring

  I picked a secret word.

  It is a 3-letter noun in the Animal category.
  Feline mammal usually having thick soft fur and no ability to roar:
  domestic _____; wildcats.

  You have 6 guesses. Type a word, 'hint', 'skip', or 'quit'.

  Guess 1/6 > dog
  DOG              [#####-------------]  26.7/100  Cool

  Guess 2/6 > lion
  LION             [#########---------]  49.8/100  Warm  new best
```

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10 or newer. There are no third-party dependencies.

```bat
python word_guessing.py
```

On Windows you can also double-click `play.bat`.

Other entry points:

```bat
python -m wordgame
python word_guessing.py --word cat --guesses 4
python word_guessing.py --category Animal --difficulty easy
```

## Commands

| Input | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| a word | Guess it and get a 0–100 similarity score |
| `hint` | Reveal the first letter (once per round) |
| `skip` | Give up and reveal the answer |
| `quit` | Leave the game |
| `help` | Show the command list |

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--word WORD` | Use a specific secret word (useful for demos/tests) |
| `--seed N` | Make random word selection reproducible |
| `--guesses N` | Set the number of guesses (default 6) |
| `--category NAME` | Restrict the secret word to a category |
| `--difficulty LEVEL` | Restrict to `easy`, `medium`, or `hard` |
| `--stats` | Print database statistics and exit |
| `--list-categories` | List categories and exit |
| `--no-color` | Disable ANSI colors |
| `--db PATH` | Use a different SQLite database |

## How scoring works

Each database word is converted into a sparse **TF-IDF semantic vector**:

1. The definition, category, synonyms, and related WordNet concepts are
   tokenized and lightly stemmed.
2. Terms are weighted with TF-IDF across all 700 words.
3. The vector is L2-normalized.

{"content": "# Word Sleuth

A self-contained terminal word-guessing game with a real word database and
cosine-similarity scoring.

The computer picks a common English word, writes a clue from the word's
definition, and asks you to guess. Every guess is scored by how close its
meaning is to the secret word — not just whether it is right or wrong.

```
  WORD SLEUTH
  a semantic word-guessing game
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  700 common English words | TF-IDF cosine scoring

  I picked a secret word.

  It is a 3-letter noun in the Animal category.
  Feline mammal usually having thick soft fur and no ability to roar:
  domestic _____; wildcats.

  You have 6 guesses. Type a word, 'hint', 'skip', or 'quit'.

  Guess 1/6 > dog
  DOG              [#####-------------]  26.7/100  Cool

  Guess 2/6 > lion
  LION             [#########---------]  49.8/100  Warm  new best
```

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10 or newer. There are no third-party dependencies.

```bat
python word_guessing.py
```

On Windows you can also double-click `play.bat`.

Other entry points:

```bat
python -m wordgame
python word_guessing.py --word cat --guesses 4
python word_guessing.py --category Animal --difficulty easy
```

## Commands

| Input | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| a word | Guess it and get a 0–100 similarity score |
| `hint` | Reveal the first letter (once per round) |
| `skip` | Give up and reveal the answer |
| `quit` | Leave the game |
| `help` | Show the command list |

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--word WORD` | Use a specific secret word (useful for demos/tests) |
| `--seed N` | Make random word selection reproducible |
| `--guesses N` | Set the number of guesses (default 6) |
| `--category NAME` | Restrict the secret word to a category |
| `--difficulty LEVEL` | Restrict to `easy`, `medium`, or `hard` |
| `--stats` | Print database statistics and exit |
| `--list-categories` | List categories and exit |
| `--no-color` | Disable ANSI colors |
| `--db PATH` | Use a different SQLite database |

## How scoring works

Each database word is converted into a sparse **TF-IDF semantic vector**:

1. The definition, category, synonyms, and related WordNet concepts are
   tokenized and lightly stemmed.
2. Terms are weighted with TF-IDF across all 700 words.
3. The vector is L2-normalized.
4. A guess is compared with the secret word using **cosine similarity**:
   `dot(a, b) / (||a|| * ||b||)`.
5. The cosine in `[0, 1]` is displayed as `0–100`.

Exact answers, plural forms, and listed synonyms score 100. A guess that is not
in the database has no semantic vector, so it scores 0 and the game says so.
Common semantic neighbours score higher: for example, `dog` and `mouse` score
well against `cat`, while `car` and `apple` score near zero.

This is a compact, deterministic, dependency-free approximation of semantic
similarity. It is not a neural embedding model, so it rewards shared
dictionary concepts rather than every association a person would make.

## The database

`wordgame/data/words.db` is a SQLite database with 700 common English words.
The schema is deliberately simple:

```sql
CREATE TABLE words (
    id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    word           TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
    pos            TEXT NOT NULL,
    definition     TEXT NOT NULL,
    category       TEXT NOT NULL,
    synonyms       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    related        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    example        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    difficulty     TEXT NOT NULL,
    frequency_rank INTEGER
);
```

The same data is stored in human-readable form in
`wordgame/data/words.json`. If `words.db` is deleted, the game rebuilds it from
`words.json` on the next launch.

The database is balanced across categories (animals, food, vehicles, people,
places, artifacts, actions, and so on) and difficulty levels. Each entry's
`related` field contains WordNet hypernyms and related concepts; those concepts
are what give the sparse vectors their semantic reach.

### Rebuilding the data (development only)

`tools/build_dataset.py` was used to generate the shipped data from:

- **WordNet 3.0** definitions, synonyms, and semantic relations.
- The `google-10000-english` frequency list for common-word ranking.

It needs the WordNet 3.0 database files and the frequency list locally:

```bat
python tools/build_dataset.py ^
    --wordnet-dir .tmp/wordnet/dict ^
    --frequency common-10000.txt ^
    --limit 700
```

The game itself does **not** need WordNet, the frequency list, or any downloaded
files at runtime.

## Project layout

```

play.bat                  Windows launcher
wordgame/
  cli.py                  terminal UI and commands
  database.py             SQLite schema, seeding, repository
  description.py          clue and hint generation
  game.py                 round/session state
  similarity.py           tokenization, TF-IDF, cosine scoring
  data/words.db           shipped SQLite database
  data/words.json         readable seed data
tools/build_dataset.py    one-time data preparation script
tests/test_wordgame.py    unit and CLI tests
WORDNET_LICENSE.txt       WordNet attribution and license
```

## Tests

```bat
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The suite covers database seeding, description leakage, synonym handling,
cosine properties, round state, and scripted CLI play.

## Credits and license

Word definitions and semantic relations are derived from **WordNet 3.0**,
Copyright 2006 by Princeton University. See `WORDNET_LICENSE.txt` for the full
notice. Frequency ordering is based on the public
`google-10000-english` word list.

The game code is provided as-is for personal and educational use.

Built **Word Sleuth**, a complete terminal word-guessing game.

Run it with:

```bat
python word_guessing.py
```

or double-click `play.bat`.

### What it does
- Samples a secret word from a **700-word SQLite database** of common English words.
- Generates a clue from the word’s definition, category, part of speech, and letter count.
- Accepts guesses and scores each one using **TF-IDF cosine similarity**.
- Gives 0–100 feedback with labels like `Cold`, `Warm`, `Hot`, and `Perfect`.
- Awards 100 for exact answers, plurals, and listed synonyms.
- Includes hints, skipping, replay, category/difficulty filters, and session stats.

### Files
- [word_guessing.py](word_guessing.py) — launcher
- [README.md](README.md) — setup, commands, scoring explanation
- [words.db](wordgame/data/words.db) — SQLite word database
- [similarity.py](wordgame/similarity.py) — TF-IDF/cosine scoring
- [test_wordgame.py](tests/test_wordgame.py) — test suite

### Verification
All **24 tests pass**:

```bat
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Example:

```bat
python word_guessing.py --word cat --guesses 4
```

1: """Clue and hint generation."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import re
6: 
7: from .database import WordEntry
8: 
9: 
10: def _mask_secret(text: str, entry: WordEntry) -> str:
11:     """Make sure the answer cannot leak through its own definition."""
12:     word = entry.word.strip()
13:     if not word:
14:         return text
15:     pattern = re.compile(
16:         r"(?<![A-Za-z])"
17:         + re.escape(word)
18:         + r"(?:'s|s|es|ed|ing)?(?![A-Za-z])",
19:         re.IGNORECASE,
20:     )
21:     return pattern.sub("_____", text)
22: 
23: 
24: def _finish_sentence(text: str) -> str:
25:     text = " ".join(text.strip().split())
26:     text = text.rstrip(" ;,")
27:     if text and text[0].islower():
28:         text = text[0].upper() + text[1:]
29:     if text and text[-1] not in ".!?":
30:         text += "."
31:     return text
32: 
33: 
34: def describe(entry: WordEntry, include_category: bool = True) -> str:
35:     """Generate a human-readable description that does not contain the word."""
36:     if include_category and entry.pos not in ("a", "s", "r"):
37:         intro = (
38:             f"It is a {entry.letter_count}-letter {entry.display_pos} "
39:             f"in the {entry.category} category."
40:         )
41:     else:
42:         intro = f"It is a {entry.letter_count}-letter {entry.display_pos}."
43:     definition = _finish_sentence(_mask_secret(entry.definition, entry))
44:     return f"{intro}\n{definition}"
45: 
46: 
47: def hint(entry: WordEntry, hints_used: int = 0) -> str:
48:     """Return a one-time hint that reveals the first letter."""
49:     letters = [ch for ch in entry.word if ch.isalpha()]
50:     first = letters[0].upper() if letters else "?"
51:     if hints_used <= 0:
52:         return f"The first letter is '{first}'."
53:     return "You have used your hint for this round."
54: 
55: 
56: def first_letter_word(entry: WordEntry) -> str:
57:     for ch in entry.word:
58:         if ch.isalpha():
59:             return ch.upper()
60:     return "?"

Answer concise but detailed enough.

The clue is **template-based and deterministic**, not generated by an LLM. It combines metadata stored in the SQLite database with the word’s WordNet definition.

### 1. The data is prepared ahead of time
`tools/build_dataset.py` pulls each word from WordNet and stores:

- `definition` — the WordNet gloss
- `pos` — noun, verb, adjective, etc.
- `category` — e.g. `Animal`, `Vehicle`, `Food`
- `synonyms` and `related` concepts

The selected sense is the most common WordNet sense, after validating the definition and removing inflected/proper-name entries. See [build_dataset.py](tools/build_dataset.py#L718-L765).

### 2. A round creates the clue
When a `Round` is created, it calls:

```python
self.description = describe(self.target)
```

See [game.py](wordgame/game.py#L62-L65).

`describe()` builds a two-line description:

```text
It is a {letter_count}-letter {part_of_speech} in the {category} category.
{definition}
```

For adjectives and adverbs, it omits the category because it adds little:

```text
It is a 5-letter adjective.
```

See [description.py](wordgame/description.py#L34-L44).

### 3. The definition is cleaned and sanitized
`_finish_sentence()`:

- collapses whitespace
- capitalizes the first letter
- strips trailing commas/semicolons
- ensures a final period

`_mask_secret()` replaces any occurrence of the answer — including plurals and forms like `-s`, `-es`, `-ed`, `-ing` — with `_____`, so the definition cannot leak the answer.

See [description.py](wordgame/description.py#L10-L31).

### Example: `cat`

```text
It is a 3-letter noun in the Animal category.
Feline mammal usually having thick soft fur and no ability to roar: domestic _____; wildcats.
```

The blank appears because the original WordNet definition contains “domestic cats”.

### Hint generation
The `hint` command is separate: it simply reveals the first letter once per round, via [description.py](wordgame/description.py#L47-L53).

So the clue generation is: **WordNet definition + category/POS/length template + answer masking + light text cleanup**. It is intentionally dependency-free and reproducible; replacing it with paraphrase generation would require an additional model or API.

We can define:
```
TARGET_STOP_WORDS = STOP_WORDS - frozenset("""
all another any anybody anyone anything both each either enough far few first
good last least less long many more most mostly much new next one only other
others own same several side some someone something such thing things time
two very way well ...
""".split())
```
But some are truly function words:
- "another", "anybody", "anyone", "anything", "someone", "something" are pronouns; target definitions maybe not.
- "all", "any", "both", "each", "either", "enough", "far", "few", "first", "last", "least", "less", "long", "many", "more", "most", "much", "new", "next", "one", "only", "other", "others", "own", "same", "several", "side", "some", "such", "thing", "things", "time", "two", "very", "way", "well" are content-ish. Include.
- "good" adjective; include.
- "first", "last", "next" etc.
- "two" number excluded by NUMBER_WORDS; no matter.
- "one" number excluded.
- "side" common noun; include. "area" too? It is in STOP_WORDS; "area" is a common noun and valid target. Remove "area". "part" is not in STOP_WORDS. "person" not.
- "show", "take", "use", "want", "need", "make", "get", "give", "go", "keep", "know", "see", "say", "think", "put", "let", "like", "seem" are common verbs. They should be targetable! The STOP_WORDS includes many common verbs because they are function-ish in definitions. That's a design mistake. We should allow them as targets. For tokenization, keep them as stopwords (maybe), but target filter should be only true function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliaries, determiners). Common verbs/nouns/adjectives should not be excluded.
- So explicit `TARGET_STOP_WORDS` is better:
```
TARGET_STOP_WORDS = frozenset("""
a about above across after afterwards again against all? no
...
""")
```
But if target "about" is a preposition/adverb, skip. "after" etc. Fine.
- Function words list: articles (a, an, the), pronouns (i, you, he, she, it, we, they, me, him, her, us, them, my, your, his, its, our, their, mine, yours, hers, ours, theirs, myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves, who, whom, whose, which, what, that, this, these, those, someone, anyone, everyone, nobody, etc.), prepositions (about, above, across, after, against, along, among, around, as, at, before, behind, below, beneath, beside, between, beyond, by, down, during, except, for, from, in, inside, into, like? (like can be verb), near, of, off, on, onto, out, outside, over, past, since, through, throughout, to, toward, under, until, up, upon, with, within, without), conjunctions (and, or, but, nor, so, yet, because, although, though, while, if, unless, until, when, where, whereas, whether), auxiliaries (be, am, is, are, was, were, been, being, have, has, had, having, do, does, did, doing, done, can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, would), determiners/quantifiers? "many" is a determiner but user wants it; include most quantifiers. 
- Also "not", "no", "yes", "very", "too", "also", "just", "only" maybe adverbs; could include as targets but definitions abstract. Not necessary.
- "there", "here", "where", "when", "why", "how" — adverbs/pronouns; skip.
- "one", "two" numbers skip via NUMBER_WORDS.
- "first", "last", "next" etc. not true function; allow.
- "all", "any", "some", "many", "much", "more", "most", "few", "little", "several", "both", "each", "either", "neither", "enough", "less", "least", "other", "another", "such" — determiners/quantifiers; allow (user expects many). Could exclude "another" but not necessary.
- "same", "own" adjectives; allow.
- "thing", "things" nouns; allow.
- "time", "way", "area", "side" nouns; allow.
- "good", "new", "long" adjectives; allow.
- "get", "give", "go", "keep", "know", "make", "say", "see", "show", "take", "think", "use", "want", "need", "let", "put", "seem", "like" verbs; allow.
- "well" adverb/adjective; allow.
- "yes", "no" maybe skip? "no" as determiner; user unlikely. Could include; not important.
- "not" skip.
- "very" adverb; allow? Definition "precisely as stated" maybe. Could include.
- "quite", "rather", "really", "mostly", "often", "always", "never", "sometimes", "still", "already" adverbs; allow? Abstract. But common. Fine.
- "etc", "via", "per" skip.
- "use", "used", "using" allow; `_is_inflected` may skip "used".

Expanded the database from 2,000 to **10,000 words**, including substantially more abstract and academic vocabulary.

### Vocabulary changes

- Built from **WordNet 3.0** definitions and the **frequency-words-50k** list.
- Added academic/abstract terms such as:
  `hypothesis`, `theory`, `analysis`, `method`, `phenomenon`, `research`, `concept`, `empirical`, `parameter`, `paradigm`, `discourse`, `cognition`, and `variable`.
- Added a curated priority list so key academic terms are included even if they fall just outside the normal frequency cutoff.
- Kept the earlier fixes: `many`, `much`, `good`, `time`, `way`, `thing`, and common words like `kitten` are included.

### Difficulty selection

The database is now split into balanced thirds:

| Difficulty | Words |
|---|---:|
| easy | 3,333 |
| medium | 3,333 |
| hard | 3,334 |

Use:

```bat
python word_guessing.py --difficulty easy
python word_guessing.py --difficulty medium
python word_guessing.py --difficulty hard
```

You can combine it with categories:

```bat
python word_guessing.py --category Idea --difficulty hard
python word_guessing.py --category Communication --difficulty medium
```

Difficulty is assigned by frequency rank within the 10k vocabulary: easy is the most common third, hard the least common third. Hard words therefore tend to be rarer, longer, or more specialized.

78: Each database word is converted into a sparse **TF-IDF semantic vector**:

91: well against `cat`, while `car` and `apple` score near zero.

Final answer concise but useful.

Clues are now substantially longer and include usage context.

### New clue format

Each clue can contain:

1. **Metadata** — length, part of speech, and category
2. **Definition** — the WordNet meaning
3. **Example** — a masked usage sentence, when WordNet has one
4. **Related ideas** — up to four related concepts for nouns and verbs

Example for `car`:

```text
It is a 3-letter noun (Vehicle).

Definition: A motor vehicle with four wheels; usually propelled by an
internal combustion engine.

Example: "He needs a _____ to get to work."

Related ideas: motor vehicle, automotive vehicle, wheeled vehicle, vehicle
```

Example for `cat`:

```text
It is a 3-letter noun (Animal).

Definition: Feline mammal usually having thick soft fur and no ability to
roar: domestic _____; wildcats.

Related ideas: feline, felid, carnivore, placental
```

### Leak prevention

The answer and all listed synonyms are masked in both the definition and example. The metadata and labels are also checked for accidental disclosure:

- `letter` → uses `6-character` instead of `6-letter`
- `idea` → omits the `Idea` category label
- `example` → uses `Usage:` instead of `Example:`
- `definition` → uses `Meaning:` instead of `Definition:`

It is a 3-letter noun (Vehicle).

Definition: A motor vehicle with four wheels; usually propelled by an

Example: "He needs a _____ to get to work."

Related ideas: motor vehicle, automotive vehicle, wheeled vehicle, vehicle
```

It is a 3-letter noun (Animal).

roar: domestic _____; wildcats.

Related ideas: feline, felid, carnivore, placental
```
